findings.title: Fresh Macs cannot run ticket checks
findings.description: `yt` and `Run.checks` invoke Docker with `--pull never`, but installation and `preconditions()` neither provision nor verify the required images, including the custom `yantra-rust:1.96.1` image. On a Mac without those images, the guard cannot start; the runner treats that setup failure as a failed candidate check, consumes its fix attempts, and hands the ticket off as `needs-human`.

findings.title: Agents can bypass the guard check
findings.description: `checks()` executes `ci/guard.sh` from the agent-edited clone and treats its exit code as the guard result. If a ticket scopes both engine and guard paths, the agent can commit a no-op guard alongside engine changes, making the runner accept a combination the guard is meant to reject.

findings.title: Agents can publish Mac credentials
findings.description: `agent_command()` permits Docker invocations with arbitrary arguments, allowing the agent to mount host credential directories, while `push()` publishes its commits and report without screening their contents. An agent influenced by a ticket body can read credentials from the Mac and place them in an in-scope commit or the PR report, even though token environment variables are removed.

findings.title: A failed label switch strands a ticket
findings.description: `run_ticket()` evaluates both label API calls before checking either result, so removal of `agent-go` can succeed even when adding `agent-working` fails. The startup error then returns before a `Run` exists, leaving the issue with neither label and no future tick able to select it.

findings.title: Failed cleanup restarts finished tickets
findings.description: `Run.finish` retains `agent-go` if its final removal fails three times and also retains `agent-working` to mark the failed handoff. Once GitHub responds again, `cmd_tick` selects the still-open issue by `agent-go` without excluding `agent-working`, so it starts another run; an existing remote ticket branch then produces an additional `needs-human` handoff.

findings.title: A failed GitHub write at run end leaves no handoff
findings.description: `Run.finish` executes the final comment and label writes but only logs non-zero exits before returning the requested outcome, even when the terminal label or refusal reason comment was not applied. If a write fails, the ticket or PR can lack `ready-for-human` or `needs-human` while `agent-working` may already be removed, and scheduled `tick` runs select only `agent-go` tickets, leaving the failure visible only in `run.log`.

findings.title: Agent file tools can reach the runner's git config
findings.description: The agent is allowed `docker run --rm --network none` with any arguments, so it can mount a host directory such as `$HOME` into a container and write `~/.gitconfig`. The runner's `git push` reads that global config, and the runner's fence only hashes the clone's `.git/config` and hooks, so a poisoned global setting would take effect when the runner pushes. The README states that the tool list is not a sandbox, but the rule requires the agent to have no push path, and this path gives one.

findings.title: Manual runs can be restarted by the tick
findings.description: `cmd_run()` calls `run_ticket()` without the label transition used by `cmd_tick()`, and `finish()` does not remove `agent-go`. When someone manually runs a labeled ticket, the next scheduled tick selects that still-open issue again; after the first run pushed its branch, the second run stops on the existing remote branch and marks the issue `needs-human`.

findings.title: Long discussions hide completed reviews
findings.description: `wait_for_review()` reads only the first page of 100 issue comments and check runs on every poll. Once the head commit’s Qodo comment falls beyond that comment page, the runner times out despite a completed review; check runs beyond the fetched page are likewise absent from its CI decision.
